analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek scores moderate on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield ~9% (EBIT 586 Cr / EV ~6,458 Cr) and ROIC ~19% (EBIT / invested capital) — neither clears my thresholds of 12%+ and 25%+ respectively. The business is decent quality but not cheap enough nor capital-efficient enough to earn a strong Magic Formula ranking.
key_strengths: Exceptional 9-year revenue CAGR of 23.3% and net profit CAGR of 32.5% — compounding at scale
Asset-light IT services model with strong FCF conversion: INR 515 Cr FCF vs 404 Cr net profit in FY26
Low D/E of 0.20 and 5/5 years of positive OCF — financially disciplined balance sheet
key_risks: Earnings Yield of ~9.1% (EBIT 586 Cr / EV ~6,458 Cr) is below my 12% buy threshold — not cheap enough
Finance costs surged 5x from INR 8 Cr (FY22) to 44 Cr (FY24) — acquisition debt is compressing returns
EBITDA dropped from 535 Cr (FY24) to 455 Cr (FY25) before recovering — margin volatility signals integration risk
red_flags: FY23 investing outflow of -719 Cr signals a large acquisition; OCF collapsed to 108 Cr that year — acquisition digestion risk remains
Finance cost trajectory (4→6→25→44→42→32 Cr) indicates sustained M&A leverage that dilutes true ROIC
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Mastek: EBIT for FY26 is INR 586 Cr. Using EV implied by EV/EBITDA of 9.80× on EBITDA of 659 Cr gives EV ≈ 6,458 Cr, yielding an Earnings Yield of ~9.1% — below my 12% threshold for attractiveness and well below the 15%+ I'd call compelling. ROIC (EBIT / invested capital of ~2,970 Cr) comes to ~19.7%, consistent with the reported ROCE of 18%. Both metrics are middling: decent but not top-decile. Magic Formula works best when BOTH are exceptional, and Mastek clears neither bar.

The business quality is real — 23% revenue CAGR, 32% profit CAGR over 9 years, and a capital-light model that converts earnings to FCF at >100%. However, the FY23 acquisition (INR 719 Cr investing outflow) loaded the balance sheet with debt (borrowings rose from 203 to 583 Cr), spiked finance costs, and caused a one-year OCF collapse. Operating margin at 14.1% is respectable for a mid-cap IT services firm but not exceptional. At P/E 12.8x it looks cheap on the surface, but the earnings yield doesn't yet scream "buy" on a risk-adjusted basis given integration uncertainty and moderating operating income growth in recent years.
